description:
SIZED s399 (probe-first, per the s397 queue item "size, do not start").
Blocker for t/op/try.t (28 rows, TRANSPILE-FAIL today).

    Parser2 TODO: compound 'try'      (Pl/Parser2.pm ~7521, the compound
                                       dispatch's rule-12 tail)

WHAT IT IS: perl 5.34's `try`/`catch`/`finally` (feature 'try'; still
experimental in 5.40, warns unless `no warnings 'experimental::try'`).  Real
CPAN code uses it, and Feature::Compat::Try compiles to it on a new enough
perl, so this is not a test-only feature.

PPI LEXES IT CLEANLY — checked s399, no repair pass needed:

    PPI::Statement
       Token::Word      = try
       Structure::Block = { ... }
       Token::Word      = catch
       Structure::List  = ($e)
       Structure::Block = { ... }
       Token::Word      = finally
       Structure::Block = { ... }

So the work is a statement lowering, not a lexing fight.

SEMANTICS, PROBED vs perl 5.40.3 (scratchpad try3.pl) -- these are the rows
op/try.t actually asserts, and three of them are where a naive
`eval {} / if ($@) {}` desugaring would be WRONG:

  1. `return` inside try (or catch) returns from the ENCLOSING SUB, not from
     the block:  sub f { try { return "from-try" } catch ($e) {...} "after" }
     gives "from-try".
  2. `$@` IS NOT TOUCHED.  With `$@ = "PRE"` before a try whose body dies and
     whose catch runs, `$@` still reads "PRE" afterwards.  The error reaches
     the catch block ONLY through its lexical `($e)`.
  3. `finally` runs on EVERY exit, including a loop control that leaves the
     block: `for my $i (1,2,3) { try { next if $i==2; $o.=$i } catch {...}
     finally { $o.="f" } }` gives `1ff3f`.  It also runs before an exception
     rethrown by catch propagates.
  4. `finally` WITHOUT `catch` is a SYNTAX ERROR in 5.40 ("syntax error near
     '} finally'") -- do not implement that shape.
  5. try/catch is a STATEMENT, not an expression: it has no value.
  6. The catch variable is a fresh LEXICAL scoped to the catch block.

LOWERING SHAPE (why this is small): CL gives all of it directly --
`unwind-protect` for finally (which is exactly "runs on every exit, including
a non-local one", covering rows 3 and its rethrow case), `handler-case` /
the existing `p-eval-block` error machinery for the catch, and a `let` for the
catch variable.  The one thing to be careful about is NOT binding `$@` (row 2)
-- the existing eval lowering does bind it, so try must not simply reuse that
path; and `return`/`next`/`last` must pass straight through (row 1/3), which
they do if the body is lowered in place rather than as a thunk.

SIZE: one statement recognizer + one lowering + runtime nothing-new.  The
28 rows of op/try.t plus a Pl/t battery (probe each expectation vs perl first;
the six above are the battery).  Estimate one focused session, no design
question outstanding.

BAR: corpus-diff (the shape occurs in no perl-tests file -- it is 5.34+
syntax); gate; sweep optional by the s375 cadence rule if corpus-diff is
identical; re-measure op/try.t and splice its snapshot row.
subject: op/try.t (28 rows): implement perl 5.34 try/catch/finally — SIZED s399, PPI lexes it cleanly, six semantics probed (return escapes the sub, $@ untouched, finally runs on loop control)
